analysisNote: Curated cross-contributor analysis across all six contributors. Matching is judgement, not string comparison - every cluster names the specific item it merges so the reasoning can be reconstructed and disputed. Strength describes how independently contributors arrived at the same claim; it never upgrades epistemic status.

leverageConvergence.theme: The system goal must be realized value, not issued value or activity

members.framing: Realized value as the system goal - align measures and decision rules around member value realization rather than value issued, activity alone, or breakage.
Reorient the system around member goal achievement - measure performance through worthwhile, realized value.
Take breakage off the scorecard. 'A measure you can't count is a slogan' - the intervention is the scoreboard, not a feature.
Frames the constraint as realization versus programme margin, which is the same scorecard tension.

leverageConvergence.whatConverged: Four contributors independently located the highest-leverage intervention at the system's goal, and all four rejected activity, issuance or breakage as the measure of success. Sly and Josh both placed it at Meadows #3 explicitly. Sly said so directly on the call: his first leverage point 'is exactly what you have there, Josh'.
leverageConvergence.whyItMatters: Four independent analyses landing on the same level, rejecting the same wrong metrics, is the strongest signal in the set. It is the most defensible shared foundation Team Zig has.

leverageConvergence.theme: Connected, visible value-state information is the enabling foundation

members.framing: Shared value-state information - a reliable view of what is identified, eligible, pursued, qualified, earned, pending, posted, redeemed, fulfilled or unresolved.
Restructure fragmented data and channels into an ambient loyalty experience.
One page showing earned, pending with a post date, redeemed, expiring - in dollars, not points.
A named variable in his balancing loop; restoring it is what resolves unresolved value.
The node her reliability loop runs on - visibility into points and redemptions.

leverageConvergence.whatConverged: Five of six. Sly and Josh classify it at Meadows #6 information flows; Joann, Henry and Ola each built it into their models as a named variable or capability. Nobody treats it as optional and nobody treats it as the product on its own.
leverageConvergence.whyItMatters: This is the shared dependency underneath every product direction in the set, and it is phase 1 of the sequence the team is converging on.

leverageConvergence.theme: Missing and at-risk value must be detected and resolved

members.framing: Exception detection and recovery - the primary product-action leverage point and the basis of his product wedge.
The corrective mechanism in his balancing loop - the only contributor to close the correction into a loop.
Phase 2 of her sequence: 'You can only spot a miss once you know what should have posted.'
Merchant and RTR integrations could confirm qualifying payments, update rewards and resolve missing value.

leverageConvergence.whatConverged: Four contributors include detection and recovery of missing value, and all four connect it to member trust.
leverageConvergence.whatDiffers: Sly and Henry make it the central mechanism. Joann makes it phase 2, dependent on the ledger existing first. Josh treats it as a downstream benefit of integrating data and payment rails.
leverageConvergence.whyItMatters: The mechanism is agreed; only its position in the build order differs, which the phase sequence in DV-02 settles.

leverageConvergence.theme: Consent is spent by intrusion, so personalization has a ceiling

members.framing: 'Personalization runs on consent, and consent is spent by intrusion.' Every permission paired with the capability it unlocks.
More data use raises privacy concerns, lowers trust, lowers willingness to share - 'more relevant, still in control'.
Make CDB value visible before asking members to connect accounts - a value preview, then progressive consent.

leverageConvergence.whatConverged: Three contributors independently modelled the same ceiling, two of them as a closed balancing loop. Josh reached it from the adoption side rather than the erosion side, but names the same mechanism.
leverageConvergence.whyItMatters: It is the only constraint in the set that acts on the flywheel's fuel rather than its output, and it caps how hard the relevance loop can be pushed.

leverageConvergence.theme: Learning from realized outcomes improves future relevance

members.framing: Decisioning based on realized outcomes - feed realization, failure and recovery outcomes, not only impressions or activations, back into future decisions.
Permissioned signal richness improves decisioning relevance, which improves realized value.

members.itemId: Member Data & Insight to Personalization Quality
members.framing: The learning arc of his reinforcing loop.
'BMO can learn more about what they usually spend money on.'
'More spend data feeds more analytics, which serves relevant offers.'

leverageConvergence.whatConverged: Five of six built the same learning arc into their reinforcing loop. It is the mechanism that makes the shared flywheel compound rather than merely repeat.
leverageConvergence.whatDiffers: Only Sly insists the feedback be realized outcomes rather than impressions or activations. That distinction is his alone and is the sharpest version of the claim.
leverageConvergence.whyItMatters: The team agrees the learning arc exists. Sly's refinement - learn from what was realized, not what was shown - is the part worth adopting deliberately rather than by default.

productConvergence.theme: Members must see earned, pending, redeemed and missing value

members.framing: Track - make qualification, earning, posting, redemption, fulfilment and unresolved states visible.
Easily track goal progress as well as earned, pending, redeemed or missing rewards.
Earned, pending with a date, posted, redeemed, missing, expiring - in dollars, not points.
'Track the value they have earned, and resolve missing or unclear rewards.'
'Members able to see what they are getting, their redemptions.'

productConvergence.whatConverged: Five of six, described independently in near-identical state language - including the same insistence that missing or unresolved value be visible, not only successful value.
productConvergence.whyItMatters: The most defensible product capability in the set. Five people would build it and none treat it as optional. It is phase 1.

productConvergence.theme: Surface worthwhile, relevant opportunities the member can act on

members.framing: Discover - surface worthwhile, attainable reward opportunities a member can understand and act upon.
Receive timely, goal-linked opportunities and incentives. Confirmed as his starting capability.
'Tied to spending they already intend to do.'
'If the offers actually fit their everyday spending, members might feel they are getting more value.'
Offers that state why this member is seeing this offer now - 'relevance is demonstrated rather than asserted'.

productConvergence.whatConverged: Five of six include relevance-driven opportunity surfacing as a member-facing capability.
productConvergence.whatDiffers: The qualifier differs and it matters. Sly and Henry qualify relevance by what the member already intends to buy - inferable from behaviour. Josh qualifies it by a goal the member has stated - which requires member input and consent first.
productConvergence.whyItMatters: The qualifier sets the data dependency, and therefore whether this can ship before or after goal capture.

productConvergence.theme: Same channel assumption: embedded, not a new destination

members.framing: Embedded within existing authenticated BMO and Blue Rewards touchpoints, connecting to rather than replacing current systems.
Begins in existing BMO and Blue Rewards channels and, with permission, combines BMO, loyalty, partner and connected financial data.
'Embedded within existing BMO and Blue Rewards digital channels.'
'It lives inside the BMO app, on top of the accrual engine we already have. It doesn't issue points and it doesn't set what they're worth.'

productConvergence.whatConverged: Four of six independently assume an embedded experience in existing authenticated channels, and all four explicitly decline to replace the underlying loyalty, banking or partner systems. Nobody proposed a standalone app.
productConvergence.whyItMatters: Removes a whole class of architectural argument from the team's remaining decisions.

productConvergence.theme: Member-stated goals as the organizing unit of value

members.framing: Set custom financial and reward goals, preferences and data permissions.
'Makes the unit of value the member's own goal - a trip, a debt paydown, a savings target.'

Realized value as the system goal — align measures and decision rules around member value realization rather than value issued, activity alone, or breakage. His product definition has no member-stated goal construct at all.

productConvergence.whatConverged: Three contributors organise the system around something other than a points balance. Two build it around a goal the member states; the third around whether promised value was delivered.
productConvergence.whatDiffers: Joann treats the goal as the unit of value but keeps realized value as the measurable proxy. Josh treats goal achievement as the system's organizing objective outright. Sly organises around realized value and has no member-stated goal construct — his objective is measurable from system events without asking the member anything, which is the argument that settled DV-01.
productConvergence.whyItMatters: This is the concrete product consequence of DV-01. The settlement nests them: realized value is the main variable and the measurable proxy, member goal achievement is the ultimate goal it serves. Goal capture is therefore phase 3, not phase 1 — the system has to work for members who never set a goal.

divergences.title: What organizes the system - settled

positions.position: Member value realization — did the worthwhile value the member was promised actually get delivered and become usable? Measurable from system events without asking the member anything.
Member goal achievement — did the member advance the goal they set? Requires the member to state a goal, and requires consent to combine data against it.

divergences.whyItMatters: Nesting keeps both contributors' reasoning. Sly's model stays measurable from day one; Josh's objective stays the point of the exercise. It also avoids the cold-start problem - members who never set a goal still have realized value measured for them.
resolutionOptions: Treat realization as the measurable proxy and goal achievement as the intent it serves — nest rather than choose.
Adopt goal achievement as the system goal and accept the member-input dependency.
Keep both and test whether goal-setters behave differently from non-goal-setters.
divergences.recommendedNext: Settled 10 Sept. Main variable: Realized Value. Ultimate goal: member goal achievement.
divergences.resolution: Realized Value is the main variable and the system's organizing construct. Member goal achievement is the ultimate goal it serves. Realization is the measurable proxy: it can be read from system events without asking the member anything, which means the system can be run and improved before any member has stated a goal. Goal achievement is what realization is for, and it enters the product at phase 3 rather than phase 1.

divergences.title: Where the product starts — three answers that turn out to be three phases

positions.position: Start with the ledger. Six value states, six failure modes, one capability each. 'Make it true' — everything else needs the state model to exist first.
Start with real-time status visibility. Her reliability loop (TR4) runs on members being able to see where value stands.
Start at the end of the chain. Proactive Value Assurance and Recovery: detect at-risk value, resolve or route it, verify realization.
Start at the front. Goal-linked opportunity surfacing — confirmed 10 Sept, not inferred.
No explicit starting point; his definition spans discovery, comparison, tracking and resolution.
Relevance with member control — 'easier and more relevant to use, while still giving members control'.

divergences.whyItMatters: With Josh's wedge confirmed, the positions are genuinely different rather than ambiguous. But they are not competing: they sit in dependency order. You cannot detect that value is missing until you know what should have posted, and you cannot personalize credibly until delivery is reliable enough to have earned the consent that personalization runs on.
resolutionOptions: Adopt Joann's four-phase sequence, which already contains every other position as a phase.
Pick one wedge and treat the others as later releases without a stated dependency argument.
Run discovery and recovery in parallel and accept the consent risk.
divergences.recommendedNext: Joann's phasing resolves this without anyone losing their position: 1 Make it true (the ledger — Joann, Ola) · 2 Make it safe (missing-value detection — Sly) · 3 Make it relevant (goal-linked surfacing — Josh, Lia) · 4 Make it wider (beyond BMO's channels — Josh's CDB loop). Henry's definition spans phases 1 to 3. Put this to the team as a sequencing proposal rather than a choice between wedges.

synthesis.headline: Four phases, and every contributor's starting point is already one of them.

phases.name: Make it true
phases.what: The six-state ledger. Earned, pending, posted, redeemed, missing, expiring — in dollars.

phases.name: Make it safe
phases.what: Missing-value detection and recovery. Only possible once the state model exists.

phases.name: Make it relevant
phases.what: Goal-linked opportunity surfacing. Spends the trust that phases 1 and 2 earn.

phases.name: Make it wider
phases.what: Context beyond BMO's own channels. Needs consent, which needs a record of trustworthiness.

synthesis.note: The sequence is not a compromise. Each phase is a precondition for the next, and each maps to a loop the team converged on independently.

divergences.title: Boundary conflict: is consumer-driven banking inside the system?

positions.position: Boundary covers the loyalty program, its partners, and its service pathways. No CDB, cross-bank data, or payment-rail variable exists in the model.
Boundary includes consumer-driven banking, authorized cross-bank data, ISO 20022 payment information, RTR and merchant integrations.

divergences.whyItMatters: This is not a difference of opinion inside one system — the two contributors are modelling systems of different size. Merging nodes and relationships across a boundary mismatch produces a map that is internally inconsistent, which is why this blocks the structural merge rather than merely qualifying it.
resolutionOptions: Adopt the wider boundary and add CDB constructs to the shared map as hypothesis-status.
Keep the narrower boundary and record CDB as an external influence outside it.
Model CDB as a named future-state extension with its own view.
divergences.recommendedNext: Settle this before merging any nodes or relationships. Sly's V2 contract already has a boundary section and an 'Outside the Boundary' view that can hold the wider constructs without committing to them.

divergences.title: Is personalization learning reinforcing or balancing?

positions.position: Learning from realized outcomes sits inside R1 and compounds — better outcomes produce better information, which produces better decisions.
Personalization learning is attached to B2 — Personalized Value & Breakage — a balancing loop that would stabilise rather than compound.

divergences.whyItMatters: The same mechanism cannot be both without a difference somewhere in the link polarities. At least one loop is mis-specified, or the two are describing different mechanisms under similar names.
resolutionOptions: Obtain Josh's B2 structure and compare polarity by polarity.
Determine whether Josh's 'breakage' term introduces a negative link Sly's model does not have.
divergences.resolution: Josh's balancing loop resolves to the breakage brake, not to a personalization-learning loop. The apparent contradiction came from his loop name pairing two mechanisms, not from a genuine disagreement about whether learning reinforces or balances.

divergences.title: Evidence asymmetry between submissions

positions.position: Cites external sources: Deloitte loyalty research, Canada's CDB framework, Google's UK portability rules, loyalBe.
One internal contract source; most claims are legacy evidence synthesis or analytical inference with source traceability still pending.

divergences.whyItMatters: Where the two models overlap, Josh's citations must not silently promote Sly's shared claims to 'supported'. The classification model already forbids this, but a merge performed carelessly would do it anyway.
resolutionOptions: Register Josh's sources in the contract's sources array and attach them only to the specific claims they support.
Leave shared claims at their lower epistemic status until independently evidenced.
divergences.recommendedNext: Register the sources; do not let overlap inherit them.

gaps.title: Josh's causal loop structure was not supplied
gaps.detail: Josh's document names R4 (Digital Friction & Engagement), R5 (Consumer-Driven Banking Awareness & Adoption) and B2 (Personalized Value & Breakage) as the loops his leverage points act on, but supplies no variables, links or polarities for them. Loop-level convergence with Sly's R1 and B1 cannot be computed.
gaps.ask: Variables, links and polarities for R4, R5 and B2 — Parts 1–3 of the intake template.
gaps.resolution: CLOSED 10 Sept. All three loop structures reconstructed and approved by Josh. TR6's variables and polarities were constructed by this consolidation rather than supplied by him - recorded as approved, not as evidence.

gaps.title: Loop numbering implies a team-wide loop register that is not in hand
gaps.detail: Sly's published model uses R1 and B1. Josh's uses R4, R5 and B2. Josh's numbering starts partway through a sequence, which implies Team Zig has a shared loop register containing at least R1-R5 and B1-B2 — and that Sly's published R1/B1 may or may not be the same R1/B1 Josh is counting from. If the numbering schemes are independent, two different loops may currently share the same label.
gaps.ask: Confirm whether a shared loop register exists. If it does, obtain it; if it does not, renumber on merge so no two loops share a code.
gaps.resolution: CLOSED 10 Sept. Personal numbering retired; the nine canonical codes are now the only identifiers.

gaps.title: Remaining contributors have not submitted
gaps.detail: Only Sylvester and Josh are represented. Convergence strength across two contributors is weak evidence of team convergence — a third independent agreement is what would make CV-L01 and CV-P01 genuinely strong.
gaps.ask: Remaining Team Zig submissions via the intake template.
gaps.resolution: CLOSED 10 Sept. All six contributors are represented.

gaps.title: Josh's product wedge is inferred, not stated
gaps.detail: JPM03 was marked as Josh's wedge candidate because his leverage points centre on goal-linked opportunity surfacing. Josh did not designate a starting point. DV-02 depends on this inference being correct.
gaps.ask: If you could only build one capability first, which one — and why that one?
gaps.resolution: CLOSED 10 Sept, confirmed via Joann. Josh's starting capability is goal-linked opportunity surfacing (JPM03), as inferred. DV-02 no longer rests on an inference.
